nodes.name: Proposition 7: Prop
nodes.statement: If $u_1(i-1) < u_1'$, then $u_1(i) - u_1(i-1) \geq 0$. If in addition $T(i-1)$ is central and there is a crossing, then $u_1(i) - u_1(i-1) \geq \log \beta$. On the other hand, if $u_1(i-1) \geq u_1'$, then $u_1(i) \geq u_1'$, and if $u_1(i-1) \geq u_1''$, then $u_1(i) \geq u_1''$.

nodes.name: Proposition 8: Prop
nodes.statement: If $u_1(i-1) \geq u_1'$, then $u_2(i) - u_2(i-1) \geq 0$. If both $T(i-1)$ and $T(i)$ are central, then $u_2(i) - u_2(i-1) = -\log(\alpha \beta)$.

nodes.name: Proposition 3: Prop
nodes.statement: If $T(i-1)$ is central and there is a crossing, then $u(i)-u(i-1)\geq \log\beta$. Otherwise, $u(i)-u(i-1)\geq 0$.

Proposition 5: Prop
nodes.statement:
We have the following (trivial) properties.
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item If there is a crossing, then the transmission is correct.
        \item If the transmission is correct, then the length of the true segment is increased, i.e., $t(i) > t(i-1)$, otherwise it is decreased.
        \item If $T(i-1)$ is central, $T(i)$ is not central and there is no crossing, then it follows that the transmission was incorrect.
        \item The following inequalities always hold $\alpha t(i-1)\leq t(i)\leq \beta t(i-1)$.
        
        \item For any $x(i)$, $y(i)$ and $t(i)$, inequalities $u_2(i)\geq u_1(i)$ and $u_2(i)\geq u(i)$ hold.
        \item For any $x(i)$, $y(i)$ and $t(i)$, inequalities $v_2(i)\geq v_1(i)$ and $v_2(i)\geq v(i)$ hold.
    \end{enumerate}

nodes.name: Proposition 6: Prop
nodes.statement:
We have the following properties.
	\begin{enumerate}
		\item If $T(i)$ is central, then $u_2(i)\ge 2 v_2(i)$. 
		\item If $T(i)$ is central and balanced, then $u_2(i) < 2v_2(i)+\log(\beta/\alpha)$. 
		\item If there is a crossing between moment $i-1$ and moment $i$, then $T(i-1)$ and $T(i)$ are balanced. 
		\item If $u_1(i-1) < u_1''$  (or $u_1(i-1) < u_1'$)  and $T(i-1)$ is central, and the transmission is correct, then there is a crossing between moment $i-1$ and moment $i$. 
		\item If $u_1(i-1)\ge u_1'$ (or $u_1(i-1)\ge u_1''$) and there is a crossing between moment $i-1$ and moment $i$, then $T(i)$ is central. 
		\item If $u_1(i-1)\ge u_1''$ and there is a crossing between moment $i-1$ and $i$, then $T(i-1)$ is central and $T(i)$ is central. 
		\item If $u_2(i)\ge u_2'$ and there is either a crossing between moment $i-1$ and moment $i$, or a crossing between moment $i$ and moment $i+1$, then $T(i)$ is central. 
	\end{enumerate}

nodes.name: Lemma 6
nodes.statement: For every $\varepsilon_1 > \varepsilon_2 > 0$ there exists $\delta>0$ such that for all but finitely many $\alpha \in (0,1)$ it holds: For $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the condition $g(0,n)>\varepsilon_1 n - \log t(0)$ implies that there is a first moment $n_1$ such that $t(n_1) \geq \delta$. Furthermore, $g(0, n_1) < \varepsilon_2 n - \log t(0)$ and $g(n_1,n)>(\varepsilon_1-\varepsilon_2)n$.

nodes.name: Lemma 7
nodes.statement: Let $\alpha$ and $\beta$ satisfy~(3). Then there exists a constant $c>0$ depending only on $\alpha,\beta$ and $t(n_1)$ such that if $g(n_1, n) > c$, it follows that $T(n)$ is central. Moreover, the length of the true segment at moment $n$ is $1-o(1)$ as $c\to\infty$.
